h: Holy Desire Makes Torah a Path to Humble Action

p: What is the meaning of what is written (Shir HaShirim 2:3),
'Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest,' etc.?
Why were Yisrael likened to an apple tree?" etc.
"like an apple tree among the trees of the forest,"
it is not Yisrael who is likened
but the Holy One, blessed be He;
and he should rather have brought the verse (Shir HaShirim 7:9),
"and the fragrance of your countenance like apples."
אַךְ בְּפָסוּק זֶה כְּתִיב אַחַר זֶה
But in this pasuk it is written afterward,
"In his shade I delighted and sat,
and his fruit was sweet to my palate."
And here in the Gemara they expounded:
put 'we will do' before 'we will hear.'"
the "we will do" to the fruit
and the "we will hear" to the leaves.
And afterward it is written, "In his shade I delighted,"
and the shade comes from the leaves;
and after this, "and his fruit was sweet," etc.
But the matter is as we have said:
that Yisrael put "we will do" before "we will hear"
at the time of receiving the Torah,
when they were then fit to rectify everything:
אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי אֱלֹקִים אַתֶּם (תְּהִלִּים פב, ו)
and the yetzer hara ceased from them;
it is written, "and you shall guard,"
and afterward "and his fruit was sweet,"
as is said (in the Ra'aya Mehemna, Emor):
And as it says in the second Commandments,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אַחַר זֶה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ב, ד)
And as it says after this (Shir HaShirim 2:4):
"He brought me to the house of wine";
and in the Midrash (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:4):
and He gave me from there the Torah,
which is expounded forty-nine ways pure
and that is Torah she'b'al peh;
and as is said in the Ra'aya Mehemna
and this is the bread of the Written Torah,
and the wine of the Oral Torah."
And this is the precision of the wording,
"and drink of the wine I have mixed,"
and it does not say "of my wine"
"The words of your beloved are dearer to me
than the wine of the Torah"
is called the wine of the Torah
explains the words of the Written Torah,
for they disagreed in explaining the verses,
and in this there are forty-nine ways pure
and this is "the wine of the Torah."
are the words of the Scribes,
the fences that the Sages decreed;
for that is what they discuss there,
the decree on the cheese of gentiles;
כְּמוֹ חֲדָשִׁים גַּם יְשָׁנִים כוּ׳ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ז, יד)
as "new and also old," etc. (Shir HaShirim 7:14):
"and these are from the words of the Scribes"
and that is what they decreed as a fence.
But here, "to the house of wine"
in which they disagreed in explaining the Written Torah;
and in this there are forty-nine ways,
as the numerical value of ve-diglo (Shir HaShirim 2:4).
"For in much wisdom is much anger";
only the Five Books of the Torah," etc.
And it is written after it (Shir HaShirim 2:5):
וּבַזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, חֵלֶק ג מ, א)
And in the holy Zohar (on this parsha, Zohar III 40a):
וְהִיא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (סַנְהֶדְרִין צו, ב)
And this is as they said in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 96b):
'On that day I will raise up
"And therefore Knesses Yisrael, who has fallen,
'She has fallen, she shall no more rise,' etc.
who were filled at the very first
from that good wine that is preserved"
that is, the wine preserved in its grapes;
מַה עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה (יְשַׁעְיָה סד, ג)
This is the preserved wine," etc.;
שֶׁלֹּא שָׁלְטָה בּוֹ עֵין כָּל בְּרִיָּה
over which no creature's eye has had power."
And according to what is said
and they correspond to the three Shabbos meals,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא עֵקֶב, חֵלֶק ג רעג, א)
as is said (Ra'aya Mehemna, Eikev, Zohar III 273a);
and Shabbos is the bas, the daughter,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ב רד, א)
is the secrets of the Torah
that will be revealed in the future,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּמִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם תּוֹלְדוֹת, חֵלֶק א קלה, ב)
as is said (in Midrash HaNe'elam, Toldos, Zohar I 135b).
Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him
with him began the two thousand years of Torah,
is a chariot for the attribute of Gevurah,
וְאִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, חֵלֶק ג לט, א)
and it is stated in the holy Zohar (on this parsha, Zohar III 39a):
"for the Torah and the wine of the Torah
are from the side of Gevurah."
the flask brings in the wine,
the apples draw out the wine
that is, the longing for words of Torah,
as it is written, "and you shall do them" (Vayikra 26:3),
through the desire and the longing.
flasks to be sated with wine,
so that the wine should not harm."
וְהוּא עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (בְּרָכוֹת יז, א)
And this is the matter of what they said in the Gemara (Berachos 17a):
that a person should not read and learn
and then kick at his father and mother and his teacher
and at one greater than he," etc.;
"it does not say 'to those who learn them'
to those who do for its own sake," etc.
"who does not do mitzvos and good deeds";
so why did it mention "kicks," etc.,
that is, that he does not turn from evil?
And also, where is it alluded to here,
"to those who do for its own sake"?
learning too is a positive mitzvah,
one of the 248 positive mitzvos in the Torah;
and one whose Torah is his occupation
is exempt from all the mitzvos,
שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהֵעָשׂוֹת עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים
that cannot be done by others
and they do not interrupt for prayer (Shabbos 11a);
(as is stated at the end of Rosh Hashanah, 35a).
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (תְּהִלִּים לד, טו)
is in the manner of what is said (Tehillim 34:15),
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר וַעֲשִׂיתֶם אֹתָם
in the manner of what is said, "and you shall do them" (otam, read atem, you):
And this is only when one acts for its own sake,
having no other intention at all,
not even to receive reward in the World to Come,
only out of longing for the Torah,
כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוַּנִי ה׳ אֱלוֹקָי (דְּבָרִים ד, ה)
that one intends for its own sake,
only one acquires pride from it,
and with this one spoils all one's deeds.
And this is "that a person should not
read and learn and kick," etc.,
"and at one greater than he," etc.:
for if one acquires pride from one's learning,
that one did not intend for its own sake.
there are levels in the matter of lishmah;
and this is what they said in the Gemara (Pesachim 50b):
even not for its own sake," etc.,
"he comes to do it for its own sake."
And we have explained the word "always":
that one merits the intention lishmah,
that what one had attained and thought before
And this is "one should always engage"
and afterward the lishmah will itself be
and one should always hope to come to lishmah.
And this is what it says:
so that the wine should not harm"
that the Torah should not bring him,
And this is "apples to direct the desire":
that is, longing and the desire of the heart;
and this is "refresh me with apples."
that is, I am still sick with love,
for we put "we will do" before "we will hear"
and it is needed that the guarding
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא אֱמוֹר (חֵלֶק ג צב, ב)
as is said in the Ra'aya Mehemna, Emor (Zohar III 92b):
"And you shall guard and do them."
which is the sum of the Torah,
and this is "the goal of wisdom";
and similar to what we learned (Avos 3:17):
"If there is no wisdom, there is no fear;
if there is no fear, there is no wisdom."
And likewise the words of Torah of the Shulchan Aruch,
שֶׁהֵם עִיקַּר הַנְהָגַת אָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
which are the essence of a person's conduct in this world:
"When a person takes to heart," etc.,
"immediately fear and submission will come to him,
And this is the teshuvah and the fear;
וְאַחַר זֶה כָּל חֶלְקֵי הַשֻּׁלְחָן עָרוּךְ
and after this all the parts of the Shulchan Aruch,
which are the words of Torah
that will bring him to fear and submission;
and through this he will merit good deeds,
